Destiny Holidays

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
For most people life is a grind of sitting in the traffic and slogging away to pay the bills: we dream of escaping with our families on that once in a lifetime holiday. Paul Peens dreamt of taking his new bride to the Maldives, to snorkel and dive in azure waters and walk along pristine beaches. He planned for months and on the afternoon of his wedding, as he was getting dressed he received an SMS assuring him all was in order and he should enjoy his wedding day. That was the last time he believed Destiny Holidays - he is yet to recover the R64 000 he paid to them

Summary:
Destiny Holidays, run by Marelise and Vincent de Bruyn, seemed like a legitimate Travel Agency. It had good reviews and many happy clients. They were polite and efficient and employed five agents. Their website carried the Asata (Association of South African Travel Agencies) logo, which Asata CEO Otto de Vries assured viewers in an earlier Carte Blanche story, should give travellers confidence that they were legitimate.
The De Bruyns had several companies registered bearing ID numbers and addresses. They worked from an office in a shopping centre in Durbanville. But then in November last year the cracks began to show and bad reviews started popping up on Hello Peter. By May 2019 they filed for voluntary liquidation and 55 people have had their holiday dreams stolen and are R2.2-million out of pocket. There are 20 cases of fraud and theft laid against the De Bruyns across the country.
But now the wheels have come off and the 55 people have formed a Whatsapp group. They have uncovered a web of lies. The De Bruyns have done this before. Vincent de Bruyn filed for bankruptcy in 2014. Then Marelise registered a franchise with Harvey World Travel in Menlyn, Pretoria, in 2015 from which both Vincent and Marelise operated. But complaints of unpaid bills prompted Harvey Travel to withdraw their franchise. So like most scam artists when the heat is on, they move town. They moved to the Cape at the end of 2015 and Marelise registered a new company, Destiny Holidays, employing her cousin’s husband, Riaan Earle, as an agent. In 2018 Marelise opened Travel Twist, a software package for travel agencies - a booking app.


Further information:
The agents would book the flights and accommodation, and push people to pay up quickly to secure the bookings, and then pay in full long before the date of the holiday. Invoices with flight numbers and detailed itineraries were booked but never paid for. In May they were still taking peoples’ money despite the terrible reviews and having already destroyed others’ holidays. But in a letter to us, they said they never meant to defraud people of their money and feel bad and distraught and it was just their bad accounting practices! After filing for liquidation, they changed Destiny Holidays landing page to DM Travel so that they could still take bookings
Then Vincent’s step-mother opened Perfect Travel which looked like a clone of Destiny Travel, and in fact advertises Destiny Travel on its website. But Vincent declares he was just trying to help out his father who is short of money. Riaan Earle, one of the agents tried to cash in one client’s Kulula voucher on her behalf, and the scams go on. But all the websites are now down - Destiny Holidays, Travel twist, Perfect Travel and all their facebook profiles - and they of course have moved again. The lawyers have no explanation and there is no hope of ever finding their money. We are tracking them down.


Extra Budget Items:
Detective services to trace them. All the phone numbers are disconnected and they have moved from their previous rented property. I have contacted PI Wouter De Swardt to trace them, we might need to do surveillance on their suspected address and follow the wife of one Riaan - one the agents home. We suspect they live together and have traced the various addresses off facebook and other means but we may have to go to the next level to trace them which is R450 per hour for surveillance and R4 per kilometer

Script:


Establishing a new coffee shop in Gordons Bay has been tough, Yolandi and Joco Naude were desperate for a holiday, and to spend time with their extended family
Yoladi [07:58:28] Since we started with the coffee shop it's one and a half year back seven days a week that we work so you know we all just decided let's do it.
Link: 08 47 16 16/08 47 47 08 The cold stormy Cape weather is exactly what the Naude family wanted to avoid when they booked for their family holiday to Zanzibar in June a special celebration that they had saved for, for a long time
Script: They paid R140 000 for the 8 of them to spend 12 days in Zanzibar which they all were all looking forward to
Eddie [08:11:28] Doing nothing no paperwork no work nothing at all.
Yolandi [08:11:31] I heard of swimming with the dolphins so I thought we could do that
Script: After comparing quotes they decided to go with online Travel Agency Destiny Holidays, run by Marelise and Vincent De Bruyn in Durbanville Cape Town
Derek [08:01:24] Eddie you were wary of agents in general.
Eddie [08:01:27] Ja Ja because I heard of stories in the past. ….so me and my uncle we went through to Durbanville ….Everything looked very nice very nice people.
Script: Estelle Opperman won a R10 000 Kulula voucher from her company and set her heart on returning to Mauritius with her sister and brother in law, so she called Destiny Holidays agent Riaan Earle who booked her last holiday
Derek [08:52:21] Estelle you dealt with this company Destiny Holidays before.
Estelle [08:52:28] Correct Derek [08:53:29] What was the holiday like.
Estelle [08:53:33] It was awesome , The service was commendable. The agency on this side they.called me the following day to hear if I had arrived safely. [08:58:23] I had no reason to worry everything they had given me excellent service before.
Script: Paul Peens was dreaming of a tropical honeymoon in the Maldives with his fiancee Franja,
paul [06:28:21] I did initially query the legitimacy of Destiny holidays I saw on their website they had physical addresses which is in Cape Town and Durbanville. Also on the website of Destiny holidays I had found the ASATA logo and I had assumed that it was a very legit company
Link 10 28 45 15 for a period Destiny Holidays was thriving they had 5 agents operating from these officers in Durbanville. They even developed a software package for other agents called Travel Twist. But in November last year the complaints started appearing on Hello Peter
Paul: [06:29:57] two weeks before our wedding in March. I emailed Destiny Holidays to request my vouchers and plane tickets to which I received no reply.. I then finally phoned their offices where I spoke to Vincent De Bruyn and he had informed me that apparently something had gone wrong with my booking and my particular suites on the island had been double booked due to a late payment
Script: The original agent had resigned but Paul thought now it was in the hands of the boss so he wouldn't upset Franja before the wedding
paul [06:32:41] the photographer was taking pictures of the wedding. I received an SMS from Riaan Earle confirming that my booking is confirmed and that I need to enjoy my wedding because everything is in order and I apologize for the inconvenience
Script: The after-glow of a fantastic wedding turned dark very quickly – Destiny holidays still hadn’t paid for any of the bookings or flights and it was too late to rebook, Paul and Franja had to start again. Vincent promised to refund the R64 000 but Paul is still waiting
Script: Estelle paid her deposit of R35 000 in February and was waiting for Riaan to finalise the Kulula voucher bookings, but he stopped answering her calls in March
estelle [09:00:17 Then I called the landline…. And if think about it now my world kept tumbling down I sent him a message up until this day I haven't had a word from them. [09:01:59] I was literally ill for two days before I took a grasp and took a hold of myself and said something must be done
Script: On further investigation she discovered the confirmation numbers of the flights and hotel bookings were fabricated. Riaan had also attempted to use her Kulula voucher to fraudulently book a car and 5 days at Sun City which she never requested. Riaan denies this
Derek [09:21:17] Are you saying they invented fictitious flight numbers
Estelle [09:21:24] when I called the airline I called Air Mauritius they said to me that the numbers were nonexistent.
Script: Yolandi panicked one night when she realised Destiny holidays webpage had disappeared and to her horror when she visited their office in the morning they had moved. Fortunately she had the home address and while they waited for them to emerge she took pictures of their cars which became vital when the search began
Link 10.24 45 07 This is where Yolandi and her sister waited to speak to Vincent, Destiny holidays worked from here after they closed their officers , their agents had resigned because of lack of funds and all the complaints coming in, BUT they were still taking money for bogus holidays
Script: The Naude family of 8 lost R140 000 for their trip to Zanzibar
Yolandi [08:07 10 13 ] I think the saddest for me was to come home and tell my children.
Script: By May the online consumer forum Hello Peter was inundated with tragic stories like these, over 50 people from all around the county were in the same boat. Melanie Harvey in Port Elizabeth started a whatsapp group gathering a comprehensive list of names, and case numbers and was shocked to see the victims increase by the week. The biggest single lost was R241 000 for a cruise in Norway.
Yolandi [08:12:06] I think the end of the day if it wasn't for the WhatsApp group and it was just our story nothing would have happened.
Eddie [08:12:22] You know no one would take it seriously and now we can stop them at the end of the day
Script: Its remarkable what the 35 angry people combining their efforts via the whatsapp group can uncover. The De Bruyns had been in financial trouble before- Vincent filed for liquidation in 2014. They had been in the travel business since 2012 with a Harvey World Travel franchise in Marelise’s name but the licence was withdrawn after complaints from supplies. In an email to us Vincent says Very few transactions were generated and they decided to close the business as it could not afford to pay franchise fees.
Link 08 51 29 18 Then they set up in Cape Town in 2015 with Destiny Holidays an online travel agency. But the wheels started falling off late last year and she filed for voluntary liquidation in May
Script; In desperation to recover his money Paul turned to the Association of travel agents for help
Paul [I received a reply within 10 or 15 minutes from a lady from ASATA confirming that Vincent will repay the money within a week's time.
Script: That has yet to materialise. CEO Otto De Vries says they were able to recover 3 other travellers moneies but pointed out that they are a voluntary organization, and not a regulatory body with limited powers
Otto [00:01:15] we had on two occasions in fact required them to submit their financials. This first happened in November of last year and we were confident and satisfied that what they submitted met our requirements.
Derek [00:01:34] But then there were complaints in January and February surely that raised the red flag.
Otto [00:01:39] Absolutely and so immediately following those additional complaints we requested for interim audited financial statements and they were unable to deliver those which resulted in a suspension and ultimately a termination of their membership.
Link : 08 42 07 02 Vincent and Marelise say they are traumatised and never meant to steal holidaymakers money but to date at least R2.4 million is missing and 55 people have had their holiday dreams dashed
Upsound of her sobbing and crying
Script :Just before liquidating the company in May Marelise sent this voice note to Melanie the administrator of the Whatsapp group
Upsound
Estelle [09:07:21] You used my money I am sorry you embezzled you defrauded me you made me sick. It's not money that I inherited from anybody. It's hard earned money. All I am asking is they need to be brought to book.
Script: Vincent via email said it was their unsophisticated system of handwritten notes and a single bank account that got them into predicament.
09 47 39 12 Marelise and Vincent stopped responding to calls in May, they switched their phones off, they closed their officers and moved house they even took down their facebook profiles and seem to disappear from Cape life but after 3 weeks of searching we have information that they are living right here in Bellville
Script: Private Investigator Wouter De Swardt tracked them down to Marelise’s mothers home, one of the clues was the Wendy house which Marelise sent the whatsapp group to show how they were suffering
Derek Upsound How you doing? Good man. Vincent can we have a word with you.
Vincent “ No unfortunately not”
Script: Then Marelise mother arrived home
Derek- Can you explain what they have done with the money
Mother Listen they haven't done anything
No , Derek’ So where has the money gone?
No there is no money gone , please
Wouter [10:19:28] Countrywide there are 34 registered fraud cases countrywide. Of known 52 complainants 34 cases were registered of a new one so far has issued a warrant of arrest in Mattetile which is in KwaZulu-Natal.
Script: Most victims have heard nothing back from the police despite the group presenting them with the entire list of all the victims and their case numbers. Without Wouter tenacity they would still be hiding
Link 10 33 05 02 we have come to speak to Riaan Earle …..he falsified the confirmation on many bookings and took people’s money when the business was already in serious trouble
Upsound “The TV’s on and everything- jup they are all hiding”
Script: But not for much longer- the warrant of arrest was issued for Marelise as the director of Destiny Holidays, although Vincent appears to have conducted most of the business. She wasn’t at home when the police arrived but realising it was game over she handed herself in, escorted by Vincent. She was denied bail and flown under arrest to the remote town Matatiele on the Lesotho border where she was charged with fraud

Script: Yolandi panicked one night when she realised Destiny holidays webpage had disappeared and to her horror when she visited their office in the morning they had moved. Fortunately she had the home address and while they waited for them to emerge she took pictures of their cars which became vital when the search began Link 10.24 45 07 This is where Yolandi and her sister waited to speak to Vincent, Destiny holidays worked from here after they closed their officers , their agents had resigned because of lack of funds and all the complaints coming in, BUT they were still taking money for bogus holidays Script: The Naude family of 8 lost R140 000 for their trip to Zanzibar Yolandi [08:07 10 13 ] I think the saddest for me was to come home and tell my children. Script: By May the online consumer forum Hello Peter was inundated with tragic stories like these, over 50 people from all around the county were in the same boat. Melanie Harvey in Port Elizabeth started a whatsapp group gathering a comprehensive list of names, and case numbers and was shocked to see the victims increase by the week. The biggest single lost was R241 000 for a cruise in Norway. Yolandi [08:12:06] I think the end of the day if it wasn't for the WhatsApp group and it was just our story nothing would have happened. Eddie [08:12:22] You know no one would take it seriously and now we can stop them at the end of the day Script: Its remarkable what the 35 angry people combining their efforts via the whatsapp group can uncover. The De Bruyns had been in financial trouble before- Vincent filed for liquidation in 2014. They had been in the travel business since 2012 with a Harvey World Travel franchise in Marelise’s name but the licence was withdrawn after complaints from supplies. In an email to us Vincent says Very few transactions were generated and they decided to close the business as it could not afford to pay franchise fees. Link 08 51 29 18 Then they set up in Cape Town in 2015 with Destiny Holidays an online travel agency. But the wheels started falling off late last year and she filed for voluntary liquidation in May Script; In desperation to recover his money Paul turned to the Association of travel agents for help Paul [I received a reply within 10 or 15 minutes from a lady from ASATA confirming that Vincent will repay the money within a week's time. Script: That has yet to materialise. CEO Otto De Vries says they were able to recover 3 other travellers moneies but pointed out that they are a voluntary organization, and not a regulatory body with limited powers Otto [00:01:15] we had on two occasions in fact required them to submit their financials. This first happened in November of last year and we were confident and satisfied that what they submitted met our requirements. Derek [00:01:34] But then there were complaints in January and February surely that raised the red flag. Otto [00:01:39] Absolutely and so immediately following those additional complaints we requested for interim audited financial statements and they were unable to deliver those which resulted in a suspension and ultimately a termination of their membership. Link : 08 42 07 02 Vincent and Marelise say they are traumatised and never meant to steal holidaymakers money but to date at least R2.4 million is missing and 55 people have had their holiday dreams dashed Upsound of her sobbing and crying Script :Just before liquidating the company in May Marelise sent this voice note to Melanie the administrator of the Whatsapp group Upsound Estelle [09:07:21] You used my money I am sorry you embezzled you defrauded me you made me sick. It's not money that I inherited from anybody. It's hard earned money. All I am asking is they need to be brought to book. Script: Vincent via email said it was their unsophisticated system of handwritten notes and a single bank account that got them into predicament. 09 47 39 12 Marelise and Vincent stopped responding to calls in May, they switched their phones off, they closed their officers and moved house they even took down their facebook profiles and seem to disappear from Cape life but after 3 weeks of searching we have information that they are living right here in Bellville Script: Private Investigator Wouter De Swardt tracked them down to Marelise’s mothers home, one of the clues was the Wendy house which Marelise sent the whatsapp group to show how they were suffering Derek Upsound How you doing? Good man. Vincent can we have a word with you. Vincent “ No unfortunately not” Script: Then Marelise mother arrived home Derek- Can you explain what they have done with the money Mother Listen they haven't done anything No , Derek’ So where has the money gone? No there is no money gone , please Wouter [10:19:28] Countrywide there are 34 registered fraud cases countrywide. Of known 52 complainants 34 cases were registered of a new one so far has issued a warrant of arrest in Mattetile which is in KwaZulu-Natal. Script: Most victims have heard nothing back from the police despite the group presenting them with the entire list of all the victims and their case numbers. Without Wouter tenacity they would still be hiding Link 10 33 05 02 we have come to speak to Riaan Earle …..he falsified the confirmation on many bookings and took people’s money when the business was already in serious trouble Upsound “The TV’s on and everything- jup they are all hiding” Script: But not for much longer- the warrant of arrest was issued for Marelise as the director of Destiny Holidays, although Vincent appears to have conducted most of the business. She wasn’t at home when the police arrived but realising it was game over she handed herself in, escorted by Vincent. metadata.Unique Selling Point: For most people life is a grind of sitting in the traffic and slogging away to pay the bills: we dream of escaping with our families on that once in a lifetime holiday. Paul Peens dreamt of taking his new bride to the Maldives, to snorkel and dive in azure waters and walk along pristine beaches. He planned for months and on the afternoon of his wedding, as he was getting dressed he received an SMS assuring him all was in order and he should enjoy his wedding day. That was the last time he believed Destiny Holidays - he is yet to recover the R64 000 he paid to them
metadata.Summary: Destiny Holidays, run by Marelise and Vincent de Bruyn, seemed like a legitimate Travel Agency. It had good reviews and many happy clients. They were polite and efficient and employed five agents. Their website carried the Asata (Association of South African Travel Agencies) logo, which Asata CEO Otto de Vries assured viewers in an earlier Carte Blanche story, should give travellers confidence that they were legitimate. The De Bruyns had several companies registered bearing ID numbers and addresses. They worked from an office in a shopping centre in Durbanville. But then in November last year the cracks began to show and bad reviews started popping up on Hello Peter. By May 2019 they filed for voluntary liquidation and 55 people have had their holiday dreams stolen and are R2.2-million out of pocket. There are 20 cases of fraud and theft laid against the De Bruyns across the country. But now the wheels have come off and the 55 people have formed a Whatsapp group. They have uncovered a web of lies. The De Bruyns have done this before. Vincent de Bruyn filed for bankruptcy in 2014. Then Marelise registered a franchise with Harvey World Travel in Menlyn, Pretoria, in 2015 from which both Vincent and Marelise operated. But complaints of unpaid bills prompted Harvey Travel to withdraw their franchise. So like most scam artists when the heat is on, they move town. They moved to the Cape at the end of 2015 and Marelise registered a new company, Destiny Holidays, employing her cousin’s husband, Riaan Earle, as an agent. In 2018 Marelise opened Travel Twist, a software package for travel agencies - a booking app.
metadata.Further information: The agents would book the flights and accommodation, and push people to pay up quickly to secure the bookings, and then pay in full long before the date of the holiday. Invoices with flight numbers and detailed itineraries were booked but never paid for. In May they were still taking peoples’ money despite the terrible reviews and having already destroyed others’ holidays. But in a letter to us, they said they never meant to defraud people of their money and feel bad and distraught and it was just their bad accounting practices! After filing for liquidation, they changed Destiny Holidays landing page to DM Travel so that they could still take bookings Then Vincent’s step-mother opened Perfect Travel which looked like a clone of Destiny Travel, and in fact advertises Destiny Travel on its website. But Vincent declares he was just trying to help out his father who is short of money. Riaan Earle, one of the agents tried to cash in one client’s Kulula voucher on her behalf, and the scams go on. But all the websites are now down - Destiny Holidays, Travel twist, Perfect Travel and all their facebook profiles - and they of course have moved again. The lawyers have no explanation and there is no hope of ever finding their money. We are tracking them down.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: Detective services to trace them. All the phone numbers are disconnected and they have moved from their previous rented property. I have contacted PI Wouter De Swardt to trace them, we might need to do surveillance on their suspected address and follow the wife of one Riaan - one the agents home. We suspect they live together and have traced the various addresses off facebook and other means but we may have to go to the next level to trace them which is R450 per hour for surveillance and R4 per kilometer
